suite_desc: Original tasks, versioned briefs and observable checks. Explore exactly what is measured, and what is not.
draft_note: Task-specific correctness, security, multiplayer and full-game quality are not certified by generic browser smoke checks. Unqualified paid tasks are blocked.
task_limits: Automated checks cover the documented contract, not creativity, fun or general exploit resistance. Human review and task-specific qualification are required.
studio_notice: Studio runs on your dedicated Windows or macOS machine, not inside this browser. The runner discovers the official MCP tools and requires explicit consent. Real Studio playtests have not been verified in this release.
arena_desc: Same brief. Two builds. Play both sides before deciding.
arena_notice: Demo campaign: these are two internally authored variants, not two AI models. Your vote tests the Arena and is excluded from all AI rankings.
arena_brief: Collect nine energy cells. Avoid the sentinels. Keyboard or touch.
vote_saved: Vote saved. Technical fixtures revealed; no AI ranking was changed.
arena_rules_desc: Same task, randomized left/right positions, one vote per match and session, expiry and rate limits. These controls reduce casual abuse; they are not identity verification or a complete Sybil defense.
lab_desc: Inspect the trail, not just the headline score.
lab_empty_desc: An operator can run the internal fixture, inspect its artifacts and publish it as a labelled harness check. AI evaluations require provider credentials and an isolated worker.
method_desc: What we measure, how we calculate it, and where the evidence stops.
method_scope_body: Standardized model tests freeze the prompt, output budget and tools. Agentic evaluations measure a complete tool-enabled solution and require a separately qualified harness. The first implemented worker is a one-shot browser-game generator, not an autonomous development agent.
method_score: A technical score is not a fun score
method_score_body: The current smoke protocol awards 100 × passed weight / total weight. A failed blocking check caps the score at zero. Missing checks produce no score, not an optimistic estimate. Every sub-check stays visible. Human gameplay, creativity and visual quality remain separate qualitative reviews.
method_statistics: Uncertainty is part of the result
method_statistics_body: Task-macro means prevent heavily repeated tasks from dominating. A seeded cluster bootstrap resamples tasks, not correlated trials. Fewer than five distinct tasks yields insufficient evidence and no confidence interval. The five-task threshold is a conservative display policy, not a significance guarantee.
method_pass_body: For n trials and c successes: pass@k = 1 − C(n−c,k) / C(n,k). It is unavailable when n < k. Pass@1 describes observed success; it does not prove deterministic reliability. Wilson intervals are provided for independent binomial samples only. Paired task differences are calculated on common tasks.
method_review_body: Non-fixture results require two distinct reviewers who did not create the campaign and report no conflict. Complete assertions, preserved hashes and a reviewed rubric are required. An entire campaign must be published before its results enter the leaderboard. Published score snapshots cannot be silently updated.
method_limits_body: Provider aliases and infrastructure can change. Self-reported game-state hooks need visual and human verification. Public tasks can be contaminated. Human votes are not objective technical correctness. Bradley-Terry support is descriptive, with ties approximated as half wins; rank confidence intervals are not implemented.
method_independence: Funding does not buy a rank
method_independence_body: Sponsors may fund explicitly disclosed evaluations. They cannot change a score, suppress a failed assertion or select a favorable subset for an undisclosed campaign. No commercial partnership is claimed in this release.
pro_title: More context. Not a paywall on truth.
pro_desc: Core rankings, methodology and verification evidence stay open. Advanced commercial services are being prepared, not sold as already available.
free_desc: Browse models, tasks, public evidence and the technical Arena. No account required.
pro_plan_desc: Extended history, advanced reports and higher API quotas. Pricing is not configured; no subscription is currently offered.

enterprise_desc: Discuss custom task design, private benchmark campaigns and independent agent audits. Every engagement starts with a defined protocol, budget and disclosure policy.
partner_title: Help fund the evidence. Not the outcome.
partner_desc: Labs and studios may contribute API credits, original tasks or research expertise. Funding and conflicts are disclosed; editorial and scoring decisions remain independent. There are no announced partners yet.

no_campaigns: No campaigns yet. Start with the zero-cost reference fixture.
legal_draft: Operator details and legal review required before a public commercial launch. These texts are an implementation draft, not legal advice.
privacy_body: Browsing the public catalog needs no account. Essential cookies maintain a session, CSRF protection and Arena continuity. Theme preference is stored on your device. No advertising or third-party analytics are installed. Accounts store your email, password hash and preferences. Contact requests are saved only to handle your request. Votes use a keyed pseudonymous visitor identifier; raw IP addresses are not saved by application vote logic. Hosting logs may differ and must be reviewed by the operator.
privacy_retention: Export and deletion are available in your workspace. Session lifetime is seven days; the visitor cookie lasts thirty days. Anonymous match and vote retention is ninety days under the cleanup command. Contact leads are retained for 180 days by that command. Billing and scientific integrity records require an operator-approved retention policy. No marketing messages are sent without a separate configured consent flow.
terms_body: This research preview provides experimental observations, not guarantees about a model or game. Do not submit secrets, copyrighted assets without permission, harmful code or personal data in task briefs. Do not manipulate votes or attempt to access private runs. AI-generated games are untrusted software and may only run in the isolated execution environment. Paid services remain unavailable unless the operator explicitly configures and validates them.
legal_body: GameDev AI Bench is an independent working project name. No trademark or domain availability claim is made. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Roblox names identify the referenced services; they do not indicate endorsement or partnership.
about_body: We are building an evidence-first way to evaluate AI game development. The project starts with Roblox Studio and browser games. Its public purpose is to make capabilities inspectable, costs understandable and limitations visible. This release contains original tasks, a working reference harness and explicit qualification gates, not a claim of being the best benchmark in the world.
faq1a: Because no independently reviewed AI campaign has been published. We will not fill the table with illustrative numbers presented as measurements.
faq2: Can I play Roblox in this website?
faq2a: No. Roblox runs in its native application. The local runner captures receipts and evidence; browser games use a different pipeline.
faq3: Are the Arena games made by competing AI models?
faq3a: Not in this launch preview. They are clearly labelled original reference fixtures for testing the player and voting flow.
faq4: Can a sponsor influence a score?
faq4a: No. Financial support must be disclosed and has no score-editing permissions. Independent review is still required.
static_notice: Static GitHub preview. Browsing and demo games work; accounts, votes, requests and campaigns require the full server deployment.
server_required: This action requires the full application server, not the static preview.
footer_note: Independent research preview. No fictional results.
api_desc: Versioned JSON endpoints, server-side authorization and a downloadable OpenAPI contract.
api_write_note: Write operations require a same-origin session and an X-CSRF-Token. Campaign creation additionally requires an administrator and an Idempotency-Key. Runner receipts use scoped bearer credentials; payment webhooks use signed raw bodies.
